findings.text: REQ-8 bundles 'medical history' with 'the rest of the patient page'. The rest of the page already includes the appointments list, so REQ-8 overlaps REQ-7 and is not cleanly atomic.

findings.text: REQ-6 only covers a patient with neither Completed nor No-show appointments. It does not say that a single zero count (e.g. Completed>0, No-show=0) still shows as 0.

findings.text: The glossary table flags 'patient page' as not found but leaves out 'appointments list', which is also absent from the glossary yet used as a term in REQ-1 and REQ-7.

rubric_items.reason: All five acceptance criteria map to REQ-1..REQ-8. AC2 is split into REQ-2 and REQ-3, and AC3 into REQ-4 and REQ-5. Out of scope gives reasons for the follow-up action and for other placements.
Most REQs cover one behaviour a tester can check. REQ-8 bundles medical history with the rest of the page, which overlaps REQ-7. REQ-6 leaves the case where only one count is zero implicit.
Known items cite ticket lines. The only assumption (REQ-9, all-time window) is marked assumed, has a real basis in ticket L12 and goes to Q-03.
The ticket does not conflict with the baseline. The counts show no medical history and do not change closed appointments, so the artifact correctly raises no conflict.

All three questions are non-blocking and have real options and defaults. Glossary and time-window questions go to the product owner and the page-identity question goes to the tech lead, which is sensible routing.
Plain and readable, and glossary status terms are used consistently. The 'appointments list' is used as a term but missing from the glossary table, while 'patient page' is flagged.
